title: Delta-adjusted tipping-point analysis for missing outcomes
summary: The treatment effect under missing at random, and the shift in the treated arm's missing outcomes at which it would lose statistical significance.

sizing._note: Sized as the primary two-arm comparison, inflated for the expected missing fraction.

pinned_defaults: Both: within each arm, the outcome regressed on the baseline covariate among completers; each arm's mean averages observed and predicted outcomes; a shift delta added to the predicted outcomes of the TREATED patients whose outcome is missing.

Both: SE from the stacked estimating equations (each arm's regression and mean); the tipping point is the delta at which the lower 95% limit is zero, found by Brent's method (uniroot / brentq) to 1e-12.
Written out in both languages; the common alternative, multiple imputation with a delta added to the imputed values, adds Monte Carlo error and cannot be agreement-tested.
_interpretation: The tipping point is not a result to be tested; clinicians judge whether a shift that large is plausible for patients who left the trial.
